task: Generate a landscape 64 by 64 cells with real relief — hills standing well above the low ground, at least 14 cells between the lowest and highest point. Build it with the node graph, and note that a single terrain generator normalises its height field into the middle of its range: you will need to combine more than one source to get that much variation. Leave the graph on the project.
notes: Written from a failure the last round produced: an agent discovered by experiment that perlin terrain cannot be pushed to a large height range by parameters alone, and that summing two sources with combine/union is the way out. This case asks for exactly that height range, so parameter-fiddling cannot pass it. It also puts the model at a scale where hand-placement is not an option.
